extra.message: The host query parameter is concatenated into os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can inject shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary commands with the application's privileges.

The expr query parameter reaches eval(). Removing __builtins__ does not prevent Python object introspection or access to execution capabilities through loaded classes. A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can execute arbitrary Python expressions, escape the intended arithmetic restrictions, or exhaust resources.

Request body bytes or the blob query parameter, optionally Base64-decoded, are passed directly to pickle.loads(). A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can supply a pickle that executes arbitrary code during deserialization.

The fragment query parameter becomes executable Jinja2 template source through Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). When Jinja2 is installed, a caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can execute template expressions that access Python execution capabilities. The resulting HTML also includes attacker-controlled markup without escaping.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: When lxml is installed, attacker-supplied request XML is parsed with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can cause external DTD/entity resolution, including server-side local-file access and network resource access where supported by the underlying parser. Returning only doc.tag does not prevent entity processing.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The request's filter object, or its entire JSON body, is passed unchanged to MongoDB find_one(). With PyMongo and MongoDB available, a caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can supply MongoDB operators and arbitrary predicates to select records; no field allowlist or mandatory record restriction is applied. The selected document is returned through repr(doc).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The lane parameter from GET or POST is passed directly to redirect() without validating its destination host. Requests satisfying the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate can produce redirects to arbitrary external HTTP or HTTPS destinations.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The operations endpoint logs the complete Authorization header and request body at WARNING level without redaction. Requests satisfying the internal-token gate can therefore place bearer credentials and sensitive payloads into application logs, exposing them to log readers and downstream logging systems.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The count query parameter directly controls an eagerly allocated list of dictionaries, which is then serialized as JSON. There is no upper bound. A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can request an enormous count and exhaust worker memory and CPU.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The length query parameter controls an unbounded random-character generation loop and string allocation. A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can submit a very large length to consume excessive CPU and memory and block or terminate a worker.

The endpoint constructs an exception containing the absolute private_exports directory and returns its text and class to the caller. This disclosure remains enabled independently of DEBUG. The trace endpoint at lines 186-188 also returns the export directory and settings-module name. Both endpoints require INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The registered case-client-fold operations endpoint has neither login_required nor the _wrk_gate used by adjacent operations endpoints. Anonymous callers receive its case_count and internal ops_memo. The exposed values are hardcoded; this response does not contain actual owner contact records.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: If SECRET_KEY is unset, Django uses the publicly known constant 'django-insecure-change-me', including when DEBUG is false. An attacker knowing this fallback can forge Django-signed values that rely on this key. The application does not fail closed when its signing secret is missing.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The seed command creates active accounts, including a firm administrator, with the fixed password Password123. These credentials are also displayed on the login page. Any installation retaining the seeded accounts permits login with publicly known credentials; this finding concerns the supplied demo setup.

When DATABASE_URL is unset, the application authenticates to PostgreSQL using the hardcoded legalcase/legalcase credentials. The README provisions this same account. The local demo default is publicly known and remains active unless explicitly overridden.

ProfileUpdateForm permits users to change their email without verification. Client authorization then treats that editable email as the ownership key, including Client.objects.get(email=user.email) in matters/views.py:264 and documents/views.py:190. A client can set their email to another client's address and access that client's matters, shared documents, tasks, deadlines, and messages.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Disabling an account changes only is_active_account. This custom flag is checked during login but not when existing sessions access protected views. Django's is_active remains true and existing sessions are not invalidated, so a disabled user retains their previous access until the session otherwise expires.

Administrators can set require_password_change through UserEditForm, but login grants a normal session without checking it. No middleware or protected view enforces this flag. Users marked for a mandatory password change can continue authenticating with the existing password and using the application.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: UserCreateForm uses an ordinary password CharField, and user_create calls set_password() without validate_password(). Consequently, the AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS configured in settings are never applied to this creation flow, allowing weak passwords such as a single character even for privileged accounts.

user_toggle_active changes account state without requiring POST. Django does not validate CSRF tokens for GET requests, and the UI links directly to this action. A malicious site can induce a logged-in administrator's top-level navigation to /users/<pk>/toggle/ and enable or disable another account.

notification_mark_read and notification_mark_all_read modify notification state on GET requests without CSRF validation. An attacker can induce an authenticated user's top-level navigation to these endpoints, marking individual or all notifications read without consent.

api_matter_detail rejects clients but retrieves the requested matter from an unrestricted queryset without checking attorney or paralegal assignment. Any authenticated attorney or paralegal can enumerate /api/matters/<pk>/ and read unassigned matters' descriptions, sensitivity, client identity, and attorney information.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: For client users, api_documents filters only on visibility='client_shared' and does not restrict matter ownership. Any authenticated client can retrieve the identifiers, titles, categories, matter names, and version numbers of documents shared with every other client.

client_detail checks only that the user is not a client; it does not check client or matter assignment. client_list likewise starts with Client.objects.all() at line 15. Attorneys and paralegals can enumerate unassigned clients' contact details and related matter metadata; attorneys also receive their conflict notes through the detail template.

client_edit permits any attorney to load and update any Client by primary key without checking assigned_attorney. An attorney can alter another attorney's client contact information, conflict notes, status, or assignment. Changing the client's email also changes which client account receives portal access because ownership is matched by email.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: MatterForm explicitly accepts every Client as the matter's client. matter_create does not validate the selected client's assignment, while matter_edit authorizes only the existing matter before saving this field. Staff can create matters for unassigned clients or move an editable matter to another client, changing who can access its client-visible records.

DocumentForm exposes an unrestricted matter ModelChoiceField. document_create saves the submitted relation without checking assignment or archived status; document_edit checks only the original matter before accepting a replacement. Attorneys and paralegals can add documents to unassigned or archived matters or move editable documents into them. The form also reveals all matter labels.

TaskForm accepts any Matter through its unrestricted matter field. task_create saves the selected relation without authorization or archived-state checks, and task_edit authorizes only the original task before accepting a different matter. Staff can create or move tasks into unassigned or archived matters, bypassing matter isolation and read-only restrictions.

DeadlineForm accepts any Matter through its unrestricted matter field. deadline_create saves the relation without checking assignment or archived status, while deadline_edit authorizes only the original deadline. Staff can create or move deadlines into unassigned or archived matters, bypassing matter isolation and read-only restrictions.

privileged_note_create checks the user's role and the matter's read-only flag but never checks assignment to the submitted matter ID. Any attorney can create privileged notes in another attorney's non-archived matter. The GET form also discloses the selected matter's title before any object-level authorization.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: client_message_create loads the matter using a caller-controlled ID and checks only role and read-only status. It never verifies matter assignment. An attorney or paralegal can create communications for another staff member's matter; attorney-created messages are automatically approved. The form additionally exposes the unassigned matter's title.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: client_message_approve checks only the user's approval-capable role and retrieves the message from an unrestricted queryset. Any attorney or paralegal can approve another matter's draft by changing pk, set themselves as approver, and mark it client-visible. The endpoint also omits the archived-matter restriction.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: client_message_send requires login but performs no role, ownership, matter-assignment, or archived-state check. Any authenticated user, including a client, can mark any approved message as sent by supplying its ID. Because client-facing views filter on status='sent', this can expose approved-but-unsent communications prematurely.

client_message_approve changes approval state without requiring POST. client_message_send similarly changes delivery state at lines 89-92 on GET. Cross-site top-level navigation can trigger these actions using a victim's session because Django's CSRF middleware exempts GET requests.

deadline_complete updates status and completed_at without requiring POST. A malicious site can induce an authorized user's top-level navigation to /deadlines/<pk>/complete/ and complete a legal deadline without consent. GET requests bypass Django's CSRF token checks.

can_access_document permits client access to public_filing documents, although the client lists, matter template, and documented authorization rule require explicit client_shared visibility. A client can directly request a public_filing document or version ID belonging to their matter and view or download it without it being marked client-shared.

When DEBUG=True, the entire MEDIA_ROOT is served through Django's unauthenticated static-file view. Uploaded confidential document versions reside under this directory. Anyone knowing or guessing a media path can download its contents without the ownership, visibility, or audit checks in document_download.

document_download reads the entire uploaded file into memory before constructing the response. Document upload forms impose no application-level file-size limit. An authenticated staff user can upload a large document and request repeated or concurrent downloads to exhaust application-worker memory.

CSV exports write user-editable fields directly through csv.writer without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. Staff can store a formula in a matter title or number and have it evaluated when an administrator opens the export in a compatible spreadsheet application. Deadline exports at lines 62-65 and document exports at lines 80-84 have the same flaw.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: log_action trusts the first client-supplied X-Forwarded-For value without validating a trusted proxy. When the application is reached directly or the proxy preserves this header, callers can select the IP recorded for logins, downloads, and mutations, falsifying security-audit attribution.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: old_visibility is captured after ModelForm.is_valid(), which has already copied the submitted visibility into doc. The comparison therefore compares the new value with itself, preventing share_change audit entries. Changes that expose confidential documents produce only a generic update event without the previous or new visibility.

DocumentForm accepts arbitrary file types, and upload_version stores their contents under MEDIA_ROOT. When DEBUG=True, legalcase/urls.py serves these files directly on the application origin without attachment disposition. An authenticated staff user can upload HTML containing JavaScript and send its media URL to another user, executing the script in the application's origin when opened.
